MARKET.head: California table grapes stay available through December for holiday retail promotions
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: The California Table Grape Commission says grapes will stay in promotable volumes through December, after a mid-November harvest end.
Commission president Ian LeMay says steady shipments and cold storage supplies will keep the market supplied well into December.
Commission research finds 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes, versus fewer than 5% preferring imports.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade as Lynch-Bages 2005 becomes top-traded wine
MARKET.summ: US and UK buyers both upped their purchasing, the former segment reclaiming their share of purchasing
takeaways: Bordeaux led Liv-ex's latest weekly trade with a 37.4% share of purchases, and Lynch-Bages was the region's top-traded wine.
Burgundy's share fell to 15.4% from 18.4% the previous week, below a September average of 24.6%.
US buyers accounted for 66.2% of Bordeaux's traded value, while the US share of Tuscan and Piedmontese trade rose to 9.6%.

MARKET.head: Surrey funds 17 rural projects, including a vineyard bird-repelling laser
MARKET.summ: A wine producer using bird-repelling lasers and cattle farmer using GPS collars to track livestock are among 17 innovative projects funded from a £500,000 pot to boost Surrey’s rural economy. Surrey County Council’s Farming Innovation Accelerator supports farmers and growers with funding for projects to modernise operations,...
takeaways: Surrey County Council's Farming Innovation Accelerator is funding 17 rural and farming projects from a £500,000 pot.
Each recipient gets a grant of up to £35,000 plus bespoke expert support, from UK government Shared Prosperity Funding.
Albury Vineyard will install an automated bird-repellent laser to protect 18 acres of vines, adding over 1,700 bottles a year.

CULTURE.head: Volcanic soils give wines a distinctive tension, shaped by harsh farming conditions
CULTURE.summ:
Vines on volcanic soil are hard to grow and their grapes are hard-won, but it all combines to produce wines with a very particular sense of place

Good stories need jeopardy. Take The Princess Bride, one of my favourite films, which I recently introduced...
takeaways: Columnist says volcanic wines share a tension and mineral character, though volcanic soils vary widely in type and climate.
Importer Nic Rizzi says volcanic wines carry an extra tension, which he links to the difficult farming on sites like La Palma.
La Palma vineyards use black ash soils, grow above the cloud layer at 1,200m, and were hit by a 2021 eruption during harvest.

CULTURE.head: Plumpton College offers Level 3 viticulture apprenticeship for UK vineyards, cohort starts 9 November
CULTURE.summ: Develop the skills your business needs, invest in emerging talent and help shape the future of the UK wine industry with a Viticulture Apprenticeship at Plumpton College. As the UK wine industry continues to grow, developing a skilled workforce is essential to its long-term success. Plumpton College’s Level 3 Viticulture...
takeaways: Plumpton College is recruiting its next Level 3 Viticulture Apprenticeship cohort, commencing 9 November, with late joiners possibly accepted in January.
For eligible non-levy-paying SMEs, 100% of training costs are government-funded for apprentices aged 16 to 24, subject to funding rules.
The programme combines workplace experience with college block weeks and is endorsed by WineGB and land-based sector bodies.

CULTURE.head: Navarra's costly rosé methods become premium selling point, English producers urged to follow
CULTURE.summ: How Navarra Rosado turned production challenges into premium positioning and a compelling marketing story. Andrea Ontiveros Flores, a sommelier and marketing & communications specialist from Alicante, Spain asks if English wine could do the same? Consumers rarely pay more simply because winemaking is difficult.
takeaways: Navarra rosado producers use the Saignée method, which can require up to three times more grapes than standard red production.
D.O. Navarra introduced the Rosado Tradition designation, requiring Saignée and exclusive use of Garnacha.

SCIENCE.head: Pembrokeshire's Velfrey wins first Welsh trophy at Glass of Bubbly Awards
SCIENCE.summ: Pembrokeshire vineyard wins prestigious Glass of Bubbly trophy and gold medal, plus two silvers, competing against Champagne and sparkling wines from around the world A family-run vineyard in Pembrokeshire has
takeaways: Velfrey Vineyard, a family-run Pembrokeshire producer, won gold and the Winter Warmer Trophy at the Glass of Bubbly Awards 2026 in London.
Velfrey's Cuvée Reserve 2022 is the first Welsh wine ever to win a Glass of Bubbly trophy, judged blind against Champagne and sparkling wines.
Velfrey Rhosyn 2023 and Velfrey NV each won silver, giving the vineyard medals for all three wines entered.

SCIENCE.head: Enartis explains matching oak alternatives to specific winemaking objectives
SCIENCE.summ: Oak remains one of the most powerful tools available to winemakers for shaping wine style, structure, and complexity. While traditional barrel ageing continues to play an important role, modern oak alternatives offer greater flexibility, lower cost, and increased precision when used with a clearly defined objective.
takeaways: Oak alternatives differ in extraction rate, toast level and sensory impact, so product choice depends on the style goal.
Oak chips added during fermentation do little for colour stability because oxygen is scarce then.
Colour stability benefits most when oak is combined with controlled oxygen exposure, such as micro-oxygenation, during maturation.

SCIENCE.head: English vineyards hit by 2026 frosts, then record heat and drought
SCIENCE.summ: With harvest complete, or nearing completion on many vineyards, Hutchinsons agronomists Rob Saunders and Will Robinson look at the impact of the record-breaking summer and what we can learn for future seasons. While 2026 could be remembered as a vintage season for some growers, others will look back less fondly, having first...
takeaways: Fifty-four Met Office stations broke their all-time daily maximum temperature records in England this summer, peaking at 38.2°C in Gloucestershire in August.
Harvest ran about 10-14 days early, with Sauvignon Blanc having a standout year while Bacchus struggled with heat and UV.
Viticulturist Markus Keller says vine photosynthesis drops sharply once leaf temperatures reach 40-45°C, and brief extreme heat is worse than prolonged moderate heat.

SCIENCE.head: UK vineyards navigate early, hot, dry 2026 harvest after frost
SCIENCE.summ: After a run of dramatically different vintages, 2026 has given UK viticulture another season that challenged assumptions, but also demonstrated just how much English and Welsh vineyards can achieve. The 2026 growing season began with a series of extraordinary frost events, creating a challenging start before developing into a...
takeaways: The 2026 English and Welsh growing season began with severe frost, then turned warm and dry with rapid ripening.
Harvest came several weeks early at some vineyards, while dry weather kept disease pressure low and fruit healthy.
Growers now face heat and water stress, so they are adapting soil, canopy and maturity monitoring to build resilience yearly.

SCIENCE.head: Domaine Bousquet details organic and water-saving practices at Mendoza winery
SCIENCE.summ: Domaine Bousquet continues to elevate Argentine wine through generations of dedication and innovation in organic wine practices. Earlier this year, Irma Remigio and her team warmly welcomed SWR’s Membership Manager, Ilva Fridenberga, to their winery. The winery, located at the foot of the Andes Mountains, is globally recognized...
takeaways: SWR membership manager Ilva Fridenberga visited Domaine Bousquet, a winery at the foot of the Andes in Mendoza, in February.
The winery is trialling biodiversity and garden vineyard corridors, harvesting from outside the vine rows in the biodiversity sections.
It switched to high-pressure hoses for cleaning harvest boxes after comparing water use, and it is working to cut bottle weight below 420g.

SCIENCE.head: MODIS satellite data validated for mapping vineyard water use in Northeast Italy
SCIENCE.summ: In North-Eastern Italy water demand for vineyards irrigation is constantly increasing, but this conflicts with the high civil and industrial rates of water consumptions in the area, which is one of the most densely populated in Europe
takeaways: Researchers at the University of Padova used MODIS satellite data to estimate evapotranspiration in a 25-hectare Italian vineyard.
Estimates were calibrated on two years of data and independently validated against four years of eddy-covariance measurements.
Results matched in-situ observations, suggesting MODIS could monitor vineyard water consumption at the regional scale.

SCIENCE.head: Rootstocks and irrigation shape Grenache water use in NE Spain trial
SCIENCE.summ: Under the context of global change, any decrease in water use by crops is essential, because water is becoming a more and more scarce resource, especially in Mediterranean areas, where grapevines are grown
takeaways: Three-year-old Grenache vines on 110-R, 41-B and 161-49C rootstocks were tested irrigated and non-irrigated in NE Spain.
Non-irrigated vines had higher water use efficiency, and 110-R and 41-B outperformed 161-49C.
Stomatal conductance differences from irrigation persisted through the season, suggesting hormonal signals may matter more than hydraulic ones.

SCIENCE.head: Italian researchers outline viticulture strategies for climate change and biodiversity
SCIENCE.summ: In the globalization conditions possible future scenarios, optimistic and pessimistic are supposed
takeaways: A Pisa University paper proposes future viticulture adapting to climate change, scarce water and competitive global wine prices.
It argues vines need more stress-resistant genotypes, and that local Italian grape varieties are being recovered to preserve biodiversity.
Researchers studied Malvasia of Lazio, Cesanese d'Affile and Cabernet Sauvignon grown under the Cordon Spur of Conegliano system.

SCIENCE.head: Portuguese trial tests ethephon and manual thinning to cut Loureiro and Borraçal yields
SCIENCE.summ: Some years, climate conditions and biological events increment the fertility of vines, which can lead to over cropping and a decrease of wine quality
takeaways: A 2007 trial in Vinhos Verdes compared ethephon, Regalis and manual bunch thinning on Loureiro and Borraçal vines.
Manual thinning cut Borraçal yield about 41% and Loureiro about 26% against untreated control vines.
Ethephon at berry buckshot stage raised Loureiro sugar and lowered acidity, but Borraçal showed no quality gains.

SCIENCE.head: Vine balance defined as the match between vegetative growth and fruiting
SCIENCE.summ: Vine balance is a commonly used term in viticulture that expresses the concept of an appropriate balance of vegetative to reproductive growth of the vine
takeaways: Vine balance means a vine's vegetative growth matches its reproductive growth, ripening the crop while setting next year's buds.
Indirect measures such as yield to pruning weight ratio are commonly used, but they do not capture seasonal growth dynamics.
A dynamic carbohydrate simulation model can show seasonal patterns of growth demand against canopy carbon supply.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Unboxed: Week of 10/25/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly dig through the pile of wine samples that show up on my doorstep, asking
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Albarino? Soleri? Pinot Iskra? New White Wine Player in China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Attendees of the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai were treated to a new local white wine producer pouring smack dab in the middle of the
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Lan Yue, established in Yantai in 2021, poured six wines at the China Sommelier Summit in Shanghai.
Lan Yue planted its first vines in 2023 and recently released its first wines, including an Albarino.
Lan Yue's vineyards cover about 230 mu (15.5 hectares), with 40 mu (2.7 hectares) planted to Albarino.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Celebrating 25 years of Filipa Pato’s wines with an amazing lunch and tasting
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Flipa Pato, daughter of famous Bairrada winegrower Luis Pato, first started making her own wines 25 years ago, in 2001
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Filipa Pato, daughter of Luis Pato, began making her own wines in 2001 at age 25, now labelled with husband William Wouters.
Filipa and William farm 20 hectares across 37 plots, using biodynamics and pigs to regenerate soils in old vineyards.
Filipa uses a drone for spraying and cover-crop seeding, though EU rules currently prohibit drone spraying of agrochemicals.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker's column says the clocks drop back on Sunday, starting what she calls Kitchen Season.
Maker says November and December bring an urge to cook for others and to revive family recipes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tasting Diaries: October 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Niagara’s Cabernet Franc harvest finally gets underway, plus the bottles that made my October memorable
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Niagara Peninsula growers saw unseasonably warm, dry October weather after one of the wettest summers on record, with Cabernet Franc harvest just beginning, a little later than average.
Buttonwood Grove's 2025 Blanc de Franc from Finger Lakes' Cayuga Lake is a white Cabernet Franc, listed at $24 USD with about 10 g/L residual sugar.
Château de Fosse Sèche's 2018 Éolithe VDF from Saumur is reviewed as showing freshness and restraint in a warm vintage, with an estimated 5+ years of life ahead.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A New White Zin
NEWSLETTERS.summ: If you are not familiar with the lore of White Zinfandel , America’s greatest contribution to wine culture , you are missing out on some excellent cocktail conversation. I understand this might sound like the layup for a bad wine joke, but I’m not being facetious. White Zinfandel is as important to the United States
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: US consumers drank 49.2 million bottles of White Zinfandel in 2024, despite wine sales being at an all-time low.
Sutter Home's Bob Trinchero created White Zinfandel around 1977 when a stuck fermentation left an unusually sweet rosé.
Tim Atkin proposes a new category called "Relevé": a field blend of red and white grapes from a whole estate or region.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near Pontevedra, Galicia, ages magnums of its Albariño underwater in the O Grove estuary.
The underwater-aged Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months at 13-16C, compared with the 'Standard' bottling of about 120,000 bottles a year.
The author's experience with underwater-aged wines has been that they taste more advanced in age and less fresh than landbound counterparts.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What to Know Before This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Wine Auction
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the world's most famous charity wine auction held since 1859. Get essential tips and insights for this year's legendary Burgundy event
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune wine sale takes place Sunday 15 November 2026, with the first lot due around 2.30pm.
The 2026 Hospices crop is small at 432 barrels, 348 red and 84 white, after an early heatwave reduced yields.
Last year's sale raised €18.8 million, with Grand Crus averaging €86,290 a cask and Premier Crus €23,180.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Visiting the Vineyard in the Sky
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The extraordinary story of Domaine de Beudon in Valais, Switzerland
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Domaine de Beudon, a Valais estate at 890 metres, is run by the Granges-Faiss family, reached only by a cable car or a steep hike.
Jacky Granges-Faiss bought the domaine in 1971; Marion Granges-Faiss, a biodynamics expert, joined in 1972 and it became Valais's first Demeter-certified estate in 1992.
Jacky died in June 2016 when a caterpillar tractor reversed over him, and Marion has since become the de facto winemaker.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude published reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the 2024 Port vintage.
A follow-up post covers older vintage Ports tasted at the same event, with vintages spanning 1985 to 2022.
